title: BrightAI Raises $97M to End Scheduled Infrastructure Inspections
dek: Physical AI sensors watch power lines and pipes around the clock instead.

facts.label: New round led by Smith Point Capital
Average early warning before a failure

caption:
Utilities still inspect their gear the way the Romans checked roads: on a schedule. BrightAI just raised $97 million to change that. ⚡

The physical AI startup uses edge sensors, drones, robots and wearable AI copilots to monitor power poles, pipelines, compressors and tanks 24/7. Smith Point Capital, the firm from former Salesforce co-CEO Keith Block, led the round, and GE Vernova joined as both investor and customer. Total funding now sits at $184 million, with a reported $750 million valuation.

Why it matters: more than half of scheduled inspections find nothing, while failures happen between visits. BrightAI says its Stateful platform runs at 50,000+ locations and spots trouble about 51 days early. Founder Alex Hawkinson, who sold SmartThings to Samsung, plans to spend most of the cash on international growth.

We're tracking the physical AI boom daily at AI Parabellum. Would you trust sensors over scheduled crew visits?

post_caption:
What if crews only went out when something was actually about to break? That's the bet behind BrightAI's new $97M round, backed by Smith Point Capital and GE Vernova.

Its always-on sensors and AI models aim to replace fixed inspection calendars for utilities, energy and water companies, catching failures before they happen. 🔧
